name: Bronx Museum of the Arts
funding: $4.3M expenses (FY2025). Public: NYC Cultural Affairs, NYSCA, NEA, IMLS. Corporate and foundation: Con Edison, Bank of America, Bloomberg Philanthropies, Deutsche Bank Americas Foundation, Ford, Warhol and Luce foundations.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies and Deutsche Bank Americas Foundation are on the roster. In 2016 two executives and four trustees resigned.
records_note: Names supporters with no date and lists its trustees; no annual report or accounts on the site, Form 990s for 2001 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: Bulegoa z/b
funding: Basque Government Cultural Department, Provincial Council of Biscay, City of Bilbao; independent non-profit cultural initiative.

name: Bundanon
funding: Revenue A$14.5M and 133,513 visitors (2024-25). Commonwealth grant A$10.1M. Partners include Landcare Australia, Oranges & Sardines Foundation, Minter Ellison, ADCO and the Gordon Darling Foundation.
watch: Donor roll is individuals and family foundations, including the late Paul Ramsay. No flagged funder found.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2006-07 with financial statements, a named 2024-25 donor roll and a 12-member board list.

name: Bunkier Sztuki Gallery of Contemporary Art
funding: City of Krakow Cultural Department, Polish Ministry of Culture and National Heritage; public municipal gallery.

name: Busan Biennale
funding: 2026 edition run by the Busan Biennale Organizing Committee for Busan Metropolitan City, with BNK Busan Bank, Shinsegae, Naver and Danish, Dutch and UK cultural funds.
records_note: It posts yearly public-interest settlement filings for 2023 to 2025 and names its officers and auditors, but no annual reports or sponsor list.

name: Busan Museum of Art
funding: Municipal museum run by Busan Metropolitan City, reopened in 2026 after a 46.9bn-won rebuild; patrons' society members include BNK Busan Bank and Hwaseung Group.
watch: Curatorial dispute, Sept 2026: Korea Economic Daily called its reopening exhibition on defector and socialist-affiliated artists one-sided.
records_note: One undated page names patrons' society members such as BNK Busan Bank and Hwaseung Group; it posts no reports, accounts or board.

name: Busan Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Municipal museum on Eulsukdo, run by Busan Metropolitan City; it hosted part of the 2026 Busan Biennale.
watch: Only the building and garden have drawn criticism.
records_note: The museum site has no annual reports, accounts, sponsor list or board; it only shows an organisation chart and the governing ordinance.

name: Buxton Contemporary
funding: Opened 2018 on a gift of the building and collection from Michael and Janet Buxton (property). Run within the University of Melbourne's museums.
watch: A 2024 student encampment at the University of Melbourne targeted the university's arms investments, not the museum, so it adds no flag.
records_note: Buxton posts no reports of its own; parent University of Melbourne tabled a 2024 annual report. Buxton names Circle supporters, undated, and lists no board.

name: BWA Wrocław
funding: Municipal gallery network of the City of Wrocław.
records_note: Its public bulletin posts annual reports 2021 to 2025 naming grant funders; budget shares only, no full accounts, and no governing board is listed.

name: CA2M Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo
funding: Funded by the Comunidad de Madrid.
records_note: Its transparency page holds only a 2024 organigram and budget; it posts no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: CA2M (Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo)
funding: Funded by the Comunidad de Madrid.

name: Contemporary Art Centre (CAC / ŠMC)
funding: Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Lithuania; public non-profit kunsthalle.
watch: Largest contemporary art space in the Baltic states and home of the Baltic Triennial. A public institution.
